Train the same classifier several times and summarise the metrics

Source: R/birdnet_train.R
pam_birdnet_train_repeat.Rd

Each run uses a different random validation split and initialisation, so a single score can be lucky or unlucky. Repeating the run shows how much the metrics vary, which is the yardstick for comparing settings, or pamflow against the Analyzer GUI, fairly.

Usage

pam_birdnet_train_repeat(data_dir, output, n = 5L, params = list(), ...)

Arguments

data_dir

Training folder (see pam_birdnet_train()).

output

Output path prefix; run k is written to <output>_run<kk> (two digits).

n

Number of runs.

params

Named list of training parameters (see pam_birdnet_train()).

...

Further arguments passed to pam_birdnet_train() (for example test_data, envdir, live, overwrite).

Value

A list: runs (data.frame with run, status, auprc, auroc, loss, best_epoch, elapsed_min, output) and summary (data.frame with metric, n, mean, sd, min, max over the successful runs).

Details

This is a standalone tool: it is not a stage of the workflow and no workflow function calls it. Use the trained model by pointing the birdnet: section of the config at it.

A failed run is recorded and does not stop the others. With a fixed test_data folder every run is scored on the same clips, so the spread then reflects training randomness only.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rep5 <- pam_birdnet_train_repeat("E:/clips", "E:/models/Check", n = 5)
rep5$summary
} # }
